描述_ZN: The Buddha of Immeasurable Life, painted by Ding Guampeng on porcelain blue paper, Qing dynasty, 99.3 cm in length and 61.9 cm in width.　　Signed on this panel: "The twenty-sixth year of the Qianlong era, the month of the longest month. Painted by Ding Guampeng."　　Inscriptions: "White square seal of Ding Guampeng" and "painted by Gong". The seals in the collection of the Qing government include: "The Treasure of the Qianlong Imperial Inspection", "Qianlong Appreciation", white round seal, "Sanxitang Fine Seal", Zhu long square seal, "Yi The white square seal of the "Sons and Grandsons" and the Zhu long square seal of the "Secret Hall of the Pearl Forest".　　The 26th year of the Qianlong reign was 1761, so this is a fine work of Ding Guampeng in his later years.　　The picture depicts the scene of Buddha Rudra appearing in the world. In addition to the Buddha in a dignified manner, there are also religious figures such as the Four Great Vajras, Gaya, Ananda, and the Two Generals, as well as female devotees kneeling with their palms together and praying for blessings. The author has vividly portrayed the realm of "man and God are connected to each other" with profound skills, creating a solemn and peaceful atmosphere. The technique of "outlining and filling with gold" is used, using clay gold as ink on porcelain blue paper, making the picture deeply and elegantly colored. The brushwork is fine, the lines are strong, rounded and smooth, and the coat pattern, which is depicted with "nail-head and rat-tail", adds a bit of spontaneity to the regularity.
